designs.name: Guardrail Reframing: L1 lessons as post-conditions/checks, not procedures
designs.mechanism: Change ONLY the content L1 reflection writes. Today L1 emits imperative PROCEDURES ("Use the dedicated Contributors report", "Verify both visible price endpoints after sorting", "Count every visibly matching commit"). These read as a plan and, once injected, displace the agent's own plan: the agent adopts the lesson's navigation route wholesale even when its self-generated route was already correct. The reframe forces L1 to emit content in a fixed GUARDRAIL grammar with two parts and one prohibition: (1) a TRIGGER ("when you are about to answer X / before you submit"), and (2) a CHECK phrased as a verifiable post-condition on the ANSWER, never on the route ("confirm the count includes every row across all pages and next-page controls", "confirm the low endpoint is the cheapest genuinely-matching product, not a variant/accessory"). The prohibition, enforced at write time by the reflection prompt and a lint step: a lesson may NOT contain a navigation verb that names a specific UI path as the way to reach the goal (no "Use the Contributors report", "Open Repository -> Commits", "switch sort to New") unless it is phrased as "if your current view cannot satisfy the check, one place that can is ...". Injection framing in the agent prompt correspondingly changes from "Hint: <lesson>" to "Before you finalize your answer, this check has helped on similar tasks; run it against the plan you already have. It is a check to pass, not a route to follow." The agent keeps its own plan; the lesson can only append a verification step or, at most, suggest a fallback view conditional on the check failing.
designs.concrete_changes:
1) L1 reflection prompt (judge_step / extract_step_experiences): replace "write the technique/procedure that succeeded" with a template: title = the post-condition being guarded; content MUST be "Before answering <task-type>, confirm <verifiable property of the answer>. If your current view cannot show that, a place that can is <optional fallback>." Ban bare imperatives; the winning navigation route becomes an OPTIONAL trailing clause, never the lead.
2) A write-time lint (deterministic, in the L1 pipeline): reject/rewrite any lesson whose content's main clause is a navigation imperative. Rewrite "Use the dedicated Contributors report" -> "Before naming the top contributor / their email, confirm the figure comes from a per-contributor commit total for the correct default branch; the Contributors report is one place that shows it." Rewrite "Verify both visible price endpoints" -> "Before giving a price range, confirm both endpoints are genuinely-matching products (not accessories/variants) and that you enumerated the full matching set, not just the first/last card." Rewrite "Count every visibly matching commit" -> "Before giving a commit count, confirm you counted every qualifying row across all pages; if the flat list is truncated or unfilterable, a per-contributor/per-date summary view gives the same total."
3) Injection wording change (retrieval-side, no mechanism change): wrap the single retrieved item as a CHECK-to-pass with explicit "do not abandon your current plan; only add this verification," and instruct: if running the check would require abandoning a route that is already producing the answer, keep your route.
4) Outcome-based usage feedback (allowed lever, light): tag each lesson with whether, when injected, the withmem outcome beat/tied/lost vs the agent's pre-injection trajectory; down-rank lessons that repeatedly correlate with the agent discarding a working plan. This is bookkeeping on the existing single-retrieval slot, not a new memory type.
designs.why_keeps_wins: t309: nomem gave up (jumped to github.com, empty). The reframed lesson still carries the fallback clause "...a place that shows per-contributor totals is the Contributors report," so the agent that was floundering still gets the pointer and reaches "Grayson Wright." A pure check with no fallback would lose this win, which is exactly why the design keeps the route as a conditional trailing clause rather than deleting it. t136: the check "confirm you counted every qualifying row on the commit history" plus the retained "commit history is one place that shows it" still lands the agent on the 235-Commits view, and the counting check nudges the 5-vs-3 the right way; nothing in the reframe removes the navigation help that made this win, it only demotes it to optional. t66: the win came from changing the sort control and enumerating fully; reframed as "before listing the top-10 posts, confirm you sorted by the ranking the task asks for and enumerated all ten," which preserves the sort/enumerate push that beat nomem's Hot-only single URL. In all three, the fallback-route clause is retained, so no win depends on content the reframe strips out.
designs.why_fixes_regressions: The 5 regressions split into two groups. Group 1 -- lesson displaced a working plan (t126, t784, t787, t304 partially): these are fixed by the core reframe. t126: nomem's own plan (Advanced Search to genuine Canon printers, full enumeration -> $2.56-$649.99) was correct; the procedural "sort and read both endpoints" made withmem trust a narrower set and miss the $2.56 low. Reframed as a post-condition on the answer ("confirm the low endpoint is the cheapest genuinely-matching product, and that you enumerated the full set"), the lesson no longer supplies a route to adopt; it only makes the agent re-check its own $49.54 low against "is this really the cheapest matching printer," which flags the missed item. t784/t787: procedural "Use the Contributors report" is what withmem latched onto to the exclusion of falling back when the "main" branch didn't exist (t784 reported infeasible; t787 produced no answer at all). Demoted to a check on the answer ("confirm the email/follower count belongs to the top contributor on the actual default branch") plus a conditional fallback, the agent keeps nomem's own recovering behavior (fall back to master, read Contributors) instead of dead-ending on the prescribed route. t304: nomem used Contributors and counted 14; the procedural "Count every visibly matching commit" pushed withmem into brute-force scrolling the raw 2,320-commit list until it ran out of steps. Reframed as a post-condition ("confirm you counted all qualifying rows; if the flat list is truncated, a per-contributor/date view gives the same total"), it both stops mandating manual enumeration and hands back the summary-view escape that nomem used, so the working plan is not displaced. Group 2 -- loop/over-verification induced by the lesson (t385): the procedural pagination framing sent withmem into repeated page1<->page2 re-verification and it dropped N Randall. The guardrail grammar caps this by phrasing the check as a single terminal post-condition ("before answering, confirm you have recorded every qualifying reviewer across all pages") with the injection instruction "run the check once, then answer -- do not re-paginate to re-verify," which removes the re-verification loop that caused the single-name drop. Net: the 3 wins are preserved via retained conditional fallbacks, and all 5 regressions lose the mechanism (plan displacement or lesson-induced looping) that caused them, moving net from -2 toward +3. Honest caveat grounded in the taxonomy: several nearby misses (i=4,15,27,29) are D-class last-mile miscounts where withmem==nomem; the reframe does not claim to fix those and does not touch them, but among the 8 DECISIVE cases every regression is a displacement/loop case that the guardrail grammar addresses.

designs.name: Precondition/Anti-condition Lessons with an Injection-Time Applicability Gate (CONDITION-gating, not cosine)
designs.mechanism:
Keep the retrieval mechanism exactly as-is: cosine on intent still selects ONE candidate lesson. The change is two-fold and lives entirely in lesson FRAMING and INJECTION-side gating, touching neither distillation nor test-time scaling.

(1) FRAMING. L1 reflection stops writing a bare title+description+content triple. Every lesson now carries a structured contract: precondition (the observable task/page features that must hold for the lesson to help), anti_condition (features under which the lesson is known to backfire — written from the failure it caused or could cause), scope (which action it licenses), and the existing content as the how-to. The precondition/anti-condition are literal, checkable predicates about the intent and the current page, not embeddings.

(2) GATE. At injection time, after cosine picks the candidate, a single cheap LLM call is made with the task intent + a compact snapshot of the current page (the same accessibility-tree summary the agent already sees) + the lesson's precondition and anti_condition. It returns APPLY only if the precondition is satisfied AND the anti_condition is not triggered; otherwise SUPPRESS. Only APPLY injects the lesson (as today, an optional hint); SUPPRESS injects nothing, so the agent behaves exactly like the no-memory arm. The discriminator is the CONDITION match, decided by an LLM reading the actual task, never the cosine score.

This directly targets the core defect the user named: helpful and harmful lessons score alike on cosine, so cosine cannot gate. A condition predicate can: t126's lesson and t136's lesson can have identical cosine relevance yet opposite gate verdicts because one's anti_condition fires and the other's precondition holds.
designs.concrete_changes:
SCHEMA (per lesson, replacing the current title/description/content record):
{
  "title": str,                     // unchanged; still embedded for cosine retrieval
  "content": str,                   // unchanged; the how-to injected on APPLY
  "precondition": str,              // NEW: observable predicate on intent+page that must hold
  "anti_condition": str,            // NEW: predicate under which this lesson is known to hurt; empty allowed
  "scope": str,                     // NEW: the single action/decision the lesson licenses
  "source_task_id": int             // for the usage-feedback loop below
}

L1 REFLECTION PROMPT ADDITION (framing lever): "State the precondition as the concrete, checkable features of the TASK and PAGE under which this move helped — name the report/tab/control involved and the answer-shape it produced. State an anti_condition: the situation where applying this move would produce a WRONG or incomplete answer (e.g. it narrows a set the task wanted whole, or it sends you to a report that lacks a field the task needs). Keep both as one sentence each, testable by reading the task and the current page."

INJECTION GATE PROMPT (retrieval-side lever), one call, ~200 tokens in:
  Inputs: intent, page_summary, lesson.precondition, lesson.anti_condition.
  Output: {"verdict":"APPLY"|"SUPPRESS","reason":str}.
  Rule: APPLY iff precondition holds on this task/page AND anti_condition does not. Default SUPPRESS on uncertainty (asymmetric: a suppressed useful lesson costs at most reverting to nomem behavior, which is a tie; an applied harmful lesson costs a regression).

USAGE-FEEDBACK (outcome lever, cheap, no mechanism change): when an APPLY is followed by a failed task on that intent-template, append the failing task's page-feature to the lesson's anti_condition on the next L1 pass. This is how t126/t304/t784 anti_conditions get populated automatically over runs rather than needing hand-authoring.

WORKED CONTRACTS derived from the 8 cases:
- t136 lesson: precondition="task asks to count/enumerate commits and page exposes a Commits link or Repository->Commits"; anti_condition="". Gate=APPLY on t136 -> keeps win.
- t309 lesson: precondition="task asks for top contributor by commit count and a Contributors report or Commits history is reachable"; anti_condition="target answer requires a per-contributor field the Contributors report does not show". Gate=APPLY on t309 -> keeps win.
- t66 lesson: precondition="task depends on a ranked/sorted set (top N, newest) and a visible sort control exists"; anti_condition="". Gate=APPLY on t66 -> keeps win.
- t126 lesson ("verify both visible price endpoints after sorting"): anti_condition="task asks for the price RANGE of a category as-listed and applying extra Product-Name filtering would drop the cheapest listed item". Gate=SUPPRESS on t126 -> fixes regression (agent reverts to nomem's $2.56-$649.99).
- t385 lesson ("open Reviews tab, verify exact product/variant"): anti_condition="task asks to enumerate ALL reviewers and variant-verification/pagination re-checking risks dropping a listed name". Gate=SUPPRESS on t385 -> fixes regression (keeps N Randall).
- t304 lesson ("count every visibly matching commit"): anti_condition="a Contributors report giving the count directly is reachable, so manual row enumeration is redundant and error-prone". Gate=SUPPRESS on t304 -> fixes regression (reverts to nomem's Contributors path -> 14).
- t784 lesson ("use dedicated Contributors report" + branch filter): anti_condition="the branch named in the lesson (main) is absent, so branch-filtering leads to a dead end". Gate=SUPPRESS on t784 -> fixes regression (reverts to nomem path -> email found).
- t787 lesson (same Contributors/branch lesson): same anti_condition. Gate=SUPPRESS on t787 -> fixes regression (reverts to nomem -> "0"; also avoids the empty-trace failure).
designs.why_keeps_wins: All three wins pass the gate because their precondition is satisfied and no anti_condition fires. t136: the task literally asks to count commits and the page shows a Commits link, so the "open commit history" precondition holds -> APPLY -> agent goes straight to the 235-Commits link and answers 5 (nomem missed to 3). t309: the task asks for the top contributor by commit count and a Contributors report is reachable, precondition holds and the answer (a name) is a field that report shows, so no anti_condition -> APPLY -> agent finds Grayson Wright (nomem gave up with an empty answer and even tried an off-instance github.com URL). t66: the task needs the top-10 ranked set and a sort control is visible, so the "change the sort control" precondition holds -> APPLY -> agent switches to Top/All-time and returns both URLs (nomem stayed on Hot and returned only one). In each win the gate's LLM check reads the intent and sees the exact features the precondition names, so injection proceeds identically to today.
designs.why_fixes_regressions: Each regression is a coarse lesson misapplied where its anti_condition holds; the gate suppresses it and the agent reverts to the winning nomem behavior. t126: the lesson's endpoint/filter framing pushed extra Product-Name filtering that dropped the $2.56 accessory, giving $49.54-$649.99; the anti_condition "extra filtering would drop the cheapest listed item for a range query" fires -> SUPPRESS -> agent behaves like nomem and returns $2.56-$649.99 (gold). t385: the variant/pagination re-verification the lesson encouraged made the withmem run drop N Randall; anti_condition "enumerate-all-reviewers task, variant re-checking risks dropping a name" fires -> SUPPRESS -> nomem behavior keeps all 8 names. t304: the "count every visible commit" lesson sent the agent scrolling and into a raw API URL and it never sent an answer; anti_condition "a Contributors report gives the count directly" fires -> SUPPRESS -> nomem's Contributors path yields 14. t784 and t787: the "use Contributors report + filter to main branch" lesson chased a nonexistent main branch to report_infeasible (t784) and to an empty trace (t787); anti_condition "named branch absent -> dead end" fires -> SUPPRESS -> nomem paths recover the email and "0" respectively. Because SUPPRESS injects nothing, the worst case of a wrongly-suppressed useful lesson is a tie with nomem, never a new regression; the gate is deliberately biased toward SUPPRESS on uncertainty, which is why net moves from -2 (3 wins, 5 regressions) toward +3 (keep 3, erase 5). This is also consistent with the taxonomy: the 4 C_wrong_or_incomplete_lesson cases (i7/12/13/20) are exactly symptom-level lessons whose anti_condition would trip the gate, and the gate never has to solve the 17 D-wall or 5 A-no-example misses since suppressing there merely reverts to nomem.

designs.name: Applicability Bandit: per-lesson, per-precondition outcome credit assignment with contextual gating
designs.mechanism:
The core retrieval mechanism is untouched: one lesson is still fetched by embedding-cosine on the intent. What changes is that every lesson carries a learned applicability score and a set of guard-preconditions, both updated from task reward after the fact, and a lightweight gate decides at injection time whether the lesson is shown, shown-as-advisory, or suppressed.

Three parts.

(1) USAGE DETECTION (credit assignment). After a task ends we already have: the injected lesson (or none), the full action trace, and the reward (WebArena binary/must_include correctness). We compute a cheap "used" signal by checking whether the trace actually executed the lesson's characteristic move -- each lesson stores a small trigger_signature (a few UI tokens/action-verbs distilled from its content at L1-write time, e.g. for t784's lesson: {"Contributors","branch picker","filter by name"}; for t126's: {"sort by Price","read endpoints"}). used = the trace contains those actions. This turns the vague "was it used" into a matchable predicate rather than a cosine guess.

(2) OUTCOME BOOKKEEPING per lesson. Each lesson accumulates four counters over the stream: (used & reward=1) help, (used & reward=0) hurt, (shown-but-not-used) idle, and a counterfactual proxy sib_delta -- when a sibling task of the same template ran without this lesson and succeeded, that is logged as evidence the lesson was unnecessary/harmful. Applicability score = a Beta-Bernoulli posterior mean (help+1)/(help+hurt+2), i.e. Thompson-style. This is exactly the axis cosine cannot express: t309's Contributors lesson and t784's Contributors lesson can be near-identical in embedding space yet diverge in this score.

(3) GATE at injection (three states driven by the score, not cosine):
 - REINFORCE (score high, e.g. >=0.6 with >=2 help): inject as a directive hint as today.
 - ADVISORY (uncertain, 0.35-0.6 or <3 uses): inject but wrapped -- "Optional past note (unverified); ignore if the page does not match: <lesson>. Do NOT abandon a working approach to satisfy this note." This demotion is the key regression fix.
 - SUPPRESS (score low, e.g. <0.35 with >=1 hurt and no help, OR sib_delta shows a lesson-free sibling succeeded): do not inject at all; agent runs nomem.
Additionally a PRECONDITION GUARD: when a lesson hurts, L1 is asked (in the post-task reflection it already runs) to rewrite the lesson with an explicit "applies only if <observable page condition>" clause harvested from where the trace diverged; the gate then only injects if that condition token is present on the current start page's accessibility tree. This tightens rather than deletes.
designs.concrete_changes:
Schema additions to each L1 lesson record (currently {title, description, content, embedding}):
- trigger_signature: string[]  // 2-5 action/UI tokens distilled at write time; drives the "used" detector
- precondition: string|null    // "applies only if <observable condition>"; harvested/tightened on a hurt
- precondition_tokens: string[] // machine-checkable tokens matched against the start page a11y tree
- stats: {help:int, hurt:int, idle:int, shown:int}
- sib_success_without_me:int    // counterfactual: lesson-free sibling of same template succeeded
- score:float                   // (help+1)/(help+hurt+2)
- state:"reinforce"|"advisory"|"suppress"  // derived; cached

New per-task log record (post-task, appended to the stream):
{task_id, template_key, injected_lesson_id|null, used:bool, reward:0|1, divergence_action|null}
where used = trace ∩ trigger_signature != ∅, and divergence_action = first action after which the with-mem trace departs from a known-good sibling (used to author the precondition).

Update rule (run once per task at end):
 if injected and used and reward==1: help+=1
 elif injected and used and reward==0: hurt+=1; enqueue L1 precondition-tightening with divergence_action
 elif injected and not used: idle+=1
 shown += (injected!=None)
 recompute score; state = suppress if (score<0.35 and hurt>=1 and help==0) or sib_success_without_me>=1 else reinforce if (score>=0.6 and help>=2) else advisory

Gate at retrieval (after cosine picks top-1):
 if state=="suppress": inject nothing
 elif state=="advisory" or precondition set and precondition_tokens ⊄ start_page_tokens: inject wrapped advisory text
 else: inject as directive (today's behavior)

Config knobs: HELP_T=0.6, SUPPRESS_T=0.35, MIN_USES=3, advisory_wrapper_string.
designs.why_keeps_wins:
All 3 wins are preserved because their lessons accumulate help with zero hurt, so they reach or stay in REINFORCE and keep being injected as directives.

t136 (gitlab, "Open Commits"): the lesson's characteristic move (open the "235 Commits" full history) is exactly what flips 3->5. On the run that produced the win, used=true and reward=1, so help=1; across its template siblings (t304 is the same commit-counting family) it keeps scoring help whenever the full-history view is what's needed. It never appears in a hurt column for its own template, so score climbs to reinforce and the directive injection that beat nomem stays.

t309 (gitlab, "Repository->Commits/Contributors + valid filters"): nomem gave up and hit an empty github.com; the lesson's Contributors move produced the correct "Grayson Wright", so used=true, reward=1, help=1. Note this is the SAME surface topic as the t784/t787 Contributors lesson but a DIFFERENT lesson record with its own counters -- the design's per-lesson bookkeeping is precisely what lets the good Contributors lesson stay REINFORCE while the bad one is demoted. Cosine could never separate them; the help/hurt split does.

t66 (reddit, sort-to-New/All-time then enumerate top-10): nomem stopped after one URL; the lesson drove full enumeration to both URLs, used=true, reward=1. Enumeration is generically safe (it never causes the agent to abandon a working path), so it stays reinforce.
designs.why_fixes_regressions:
Each regression is caused by a lesson MISAPPLIED against a page where its precondition did not hold, and each is fixed by a specific state transition:

t126 (shopping, "Verify both visible price endpoints after sorting by price"): the lesson made the agent over-restrict to "actual Canon photo printers" (11 items) and drop the $2.56 low end, while lesson-free nomem enumerated all 33 and got $2.56-$649.99. First hurt: hurt=1, help=0 -> score 0.33 -> SUPPRESS. Reinforced by sib_success_without_me: the taxonomy's category-C entries (i=12, i=20) confirm a lesson-free sibling won this exact template, so sib_success_without_me>=1 forces suppress immediately even before enough uses accumulate. On the next Canon-range task the agent runs nomem and recovers $2.56.

t784 and t787 (gitlab, "Use the dedicated Contributors report"): both chased a nonexistent "main" branch -> report_infeasible / crashed empty trace, while nomem reached the Contributors page under the actual default branch. used=true (trace hit the Contributors/branch-picker signature), reward=0 -> hurt. Two hurts, zero help for THIS lesson record -> SUPPRESS. The precondition-tightening also fires: divergence_action = the "fill branch = main" step, so L1 rewrites the lesson to "applies only if the repo actually has a 'main' branch"; since neither repo's start-page tokens contain a main branch, the guard alone would already downgrade it to advisory even before suppression. Both revert to nomem and recover the email / "0".

t304 (gitlab, "Count every visibly matching commit"): lesson pushed raw-commit-list scrolling + an API URL, ending in '' ; nomem used the Contributors page -> 14. used=true, reward=0 -> hurt=1, and taxonomy i=7 records a same-template lesson-free... path being the winner, so sib_success_without_me triggers SUPPRESS. Agent reverts to nomem's Contributors route -> 14.

t385 (shopping, "Open the product's Reviews tab"): the lesson itself is benign but the directive framing let the agent thrash pagination and drop "N Randall"; nomem paginated cleanly. First hurt -> score 0.33 and, more importantly, until it has proven help it sits in ADVISORY, where the wrapper text "do NOT abandon a working approach / ignore if page doesn't match" removes the compulsion that caused the pagination thrash. Either path (advisory demotion on low confidence, or suppress after the hurt) restores the complete 8-name list.

Net effect: 3 wins remain injected-and-helping, all 5 regressing lessons drop to suppress/advisory and the agent falls back to its correct nomem behavior -> 3 wins - 0 regressions = +3.

designs.mechanism:
Plan-first, lesson-as-cross-check with a divergence gate ("blind self-commit, then reveal-and-reconcile"). The root failure across the 5 regressions is not retrieval and not knowledge — it is a DECISION failure made at the wrong time. Today the lesson and the agent's plan live in the same prompt turn, so the lesson anchors the plan before any independent judgment exists; the soft "use only if it fits" instruction cannot bite because the agent has no un-anchored baseline to compare against. The mechanism separates the two in TIME and forces a structured reconciliation, so a coarse lesson can only WIN when it names a concrete discriminator the agent's own plan is missing.

Concretely it is a two-phase turn on the FIRST step of each episode (and re-triggered whenever the retrieved lesson would change the next action):

Phase 1 — blind commit. The retrieved lesson is withheld. The agent sees only TASK + page and must emit (a) a short PLAN and (b) for lookup/aggregation tasks, its own PROVISIONAL ANSWER PROCEDURE ("I will search, restrict to actual Canon photo printers, then read the min/max price"). This is the counterfactual "what would I do anyway?" captured as an artifact, not left implicit.

Phase 2 — reveal-and-reconcile. Now inject the lesson, but framed as a CHECKER, and require the agent to fill a 3-slot gate before it may deviate from its Phase-1 plan: (1) DOES-IT-FIT: does the lesson's "applies when" description match the concrete objects in THIS task? (2) DISCRIMINATOR: does the lesson tell me something specific and verifiable I did not already have (a filter, an exact page, a named pitfall) — or just re-describe a procedure I already planned? (3) COST/RISK: does following it add steps or a branch that could fail where my own plan already reaches the answer? Rule: adopt the lesson's deviation ONLY if slot 2 yields a concrete discriminator AND slot 1 matches AND slot 3 is not "adds a failure branch". Otherwise keep the Phase-1 plan. Ties and vague matches resolve to the agent's own plan (self-consistency default = trust free reasoning).
designs.concrete_changes:
Three edits, none touching the core embed/retrieve/write mechanism:

1) rollout.py (WA, src/hippo/wa/rollout.py ~line 175-200): replace the single-shot mem_block+TASK+page user message with a two-call first step. Call A sends system+TASK+page WITHOUT mem_block and asks for PLAN and PROVISIONAL PROCEDURE (a lightweight schema, e.g. lines "PLAN:" / "PROCEDURE:"). Call B sends the same context PLUS the Phase-1 PLAN/PROCEDURE text PLUS the lesson, and requires the 3-slot gate (FIT / DISCRIMINATOR / COST) followed by the chosen action. Only Phase-2's action is executed. Subsequent steps run as today (no double call) unless the lesson text is present AND the model's proposed next action diverges from the standing plan, in which case re-run the gate. Cost is ~1 extra LLM call on step 1, no test-time scaling of the rollout itself.

2) store.render (src/hippo/memory/store.py ~line 136-144): change the reasoning template from an imperative ("From the project, expand Repository and select Commits...") to a checker frame that surfaces the DISCRIMINATOR explicitly: "[cross-check] If <applies-when> holds, the specific thing prior tasks got wrong/right was: <content>. Use only to correct a gap in your own plan." The "applies when: {description}" slot already exists and becomes slot-1 of the gate.

3) L1 reflection prompt (the judge_step / extract_step_experiences writer): require every lesson to emit a DISCRIMINATOR field — the one concrete, checkable fact that distinguished success from failure (e.g. "the Contributors report defaults to a branch that may not exist; verify the branch has the data before trusting it" rather than "use the Contributors report"). Lessons that can only produce a coarse procedure with no discriminator are down-weighted/not written. This directly reshapes the framing lever the constraint allows.
designs.why_keeps_wins:
The 3 wins all share a signature: the lesson supplied a concrete NAVIGATION DISCRIMINATOR that the agent's blind plan lacked, and the gate's slot-2 fires cleanly for exactly these.

t136 (3->5, gold 5): nomem clicked the "235 Commits" link and stopped at a truncated/mis-scoped count; the lesson "Repository -> Commits, choose the relevant branch" names a specific page and the branch dimension the blind plan omitted. Slot-1 fits (it IS a commit-count-by-person task), slot-2 yields a real discriminator (correct branch/full history page), slot-3 adds no failure branch -> gate adopts it. Win kept.

t309 (empty->"Grayson Wright"): nomem bailed to github.com and produced nothing; the lesson "Repository -> Commits/Contributors, select the correct branch" is precisely the missing procedure. Blind plan was empty/wrong, so slot-2 is unambiguously additive. Win kept.

t66 (1 URL -> 2 URLs, gold 2): nomem stayed on Hot and found one qualifying post; the lesson about reaching the full ranked list / comment history pushed the correct sort-and-enumerate that surfaced the second URL. The discriminator (don't stop at the Hot listing, reach the full set) is concrete and the blind plan demonstrably under-enumerated, so the gate adopts. Win kept.

In all three, slot-2 produces something the Phase-1 plan objectively did not have, which is exactly the condition the gate requires to deviate.
designs.why_fixes_regressions:
The 5 regressions all fail slot-2 or slot-3 because the agent's blind plan was already correct and the lesson only re-described (or coarsened) it — the whole point of committing the plan BEFORE seeing the lesson.

t126 (correct "$2.56-$649.99" -> wrong "$49.54..."): the lesson "verify both visible price endpoints after sorting" is a coarse procedure. In Phase 1 the agent's own plan already restricts to actual Canon photo printers and reads min/max; the lesson supplies NO new discriminator (slot-2 = "just re-describes what I planned") and its "sort then read endpoints" nudge actively drops the product-filtering the blind plan did on its own (slot-3 = adds a failure branch). Gate keeps the Phase-1 plan -> nomem's correct answer preserved.

t784 (correct email -> infeasible): lesson "use the dedicated Contributors report" sent the agent into a branch-picker dead end hunting a non-existent "main". Blind plan (nomem) reached Contributors via a different, working path and got the email. Slot-1 partially fits but slot-3 clearly flags "adds a branch that fails where my plan reached the answer" -> gate declines the deviation. With the DISCRIMINATOR-framed L1 rewrite, this lesson would instead read "verify the branch actually has data before trusting the Contributors report," which would not have triggered the doomed main-branch hunt.

t787 (correct "0" -> empty): same "Contributors report" lesson, same branch trap; the withmem_trace is empty/aborted while nomem walked contributors sorted by commit count and answered 0. Slot-3 rejects. Preserved.

t304 (correct "14" -> empty): lesson "count every visibly matching commit" pushed exhaustive scroll-and-API enumeration that never terminated; nomem used Contributors + bounded reasoning to reach 14. Slot-2 gives no concrete discriminator over the blind plan and slot-3 flags an open-ended failure branch -> gate keeps Phase-1. Preserved.

t385 (8 names -> 7, dropped "N Randall"): lesson "open Reviews tab and scroll all pages" matched what the agent already planned (slot-2 = no new discriminator); worse, the withmem arm thrashed pagination and lost a reviewer. Gate defaults to the blind plan, which enumerated cleanly. Preserved.

Net: 3 wins retained (slot-2 fires), 5 regressions eliminated (slot-2 empty or slot-3 flags a failure branch, so the agent's own correct plan stands) -> +3.
designs.name: Blind-commit plan-first with lesson-as-cross-check divergence gate

evals.design_name: Precondition/Anti-condition Lessons with an Injection-Time Applicability Gate (CONDITION-gating, not cosine)
evals.per_case: WINS (gate must APPLY, reproducing today's withmem win): t136 KEPT — precondition "count commits + Commits link visible" plainly holds, APPLY replays the win (answer 5). t309 KEPT — precondition "top contributor by commit count + Contributors report reachable" holds and the answer (a name) is a field that report shows so no anti_condition fires, APPLY replays Grayson Wright. t66 KEPT — precondition "ranked set + visible sort control" holds, APPLY. (Adversarial note: the lesson content actually says sort Hot->New while the win came from Hot->Top->All-time, so the injected hint is partly wrong-direction, but APPLY == today's behavior so the win survives regardless.) REGRESSIONS (gate must SUPPRESS -> revert to nomem): t126 FIXED — SUPPRESS reverts to nomem's $2.56-$649.99 (caveat: nomem ALSO used Advanced-Search Product-Name filtering; the real divergence was nomem picking 36-per-page and seeing all 33 rows, which is neither in the lesson nor the anti_condition — so the outcome is right only if SUPPRESS==clean nomem replay). t385 FIXED — SUPPRESS reverts to nomem which keeps N Randall; anti_condition "variant re-check drops a name" is a post-hoc gloss on a pagination-thrash failure but the outcome is correct. t304 FIXED — SUPPRESS reverts to nomem's Contributors path -> 14. t784 FIXED (weakly) — SUPPRESS reverts to nomem which recovers secupwn's email; but nomem ALSO chased a nonexistent "main" and only won via a master/Contributors fallback, so the anti_condition "branch absent -> dead end" was equally true of the winning nomem run and does not explain the divergence. t787 NOT COUNTED — withmem_trace is EMPTY ([]), i.e. a crash/harness failure, not an observable lesson-misapplication; suppressing the lesson does not credibly prevent an empty trace, and the gate itself adds an LLM call (a new failure surface). When in doubt, not counted.
evals.key_risk: The design's own regression fixes assume anti_conditions are already populated, but they are hand-derived from known failures in hindsight; the usage-feedback loop that auto-populates them needs multiple same-template runs, so on first encounter anti_condition is empty and the gate APPLIES -> the regression is NOT prevented. It also requires the LLM gate to make OPPOSITE verdicts on near-identical-cosine lessons (t304 vs t136 both "count commits"; t784/t787 vs t309 both "Contributors report"), which demands very precise anti_condition authoring and reliable page-snapshot evaluation. Finally, "SUPPRESS == clean nomem replay" is not free: t784/t787 show nomem itself barely won via a fallback the gate cannot guarantee re-triggers, and t787's empty trace shows the outcome is not always a clean nomem replay.

evals.design_name: Guardrail Reframing: L1 lessons as post-conditions/checks, not procedures
evals.key_risk: The check-not-route framing plus injection wording (keep your current plan, only add this verification, do not abandon a working route) is safe against displacement regressions but structurally weakens the single retrieval slot's ability to DECISIVELY rescue a floundering agent, which is the source of 2 of the 3 wins (t309, t136 lean on the navigation pointer). Demoting navigation to a hedged conditional fallback risks the floundering agent sticking with a broken plan instead of switching. Separately, the reframe cannot touch failures rooted in genuine filtering-judgment ambiguity (t126) or an unexplained empty trace (t787), so the claimed net +3 is optimistic; realistic net is closer to +0 to +1.
evals.per_case:
WINS. t66 (kept): win came from touching the sort control + enumerating all ten; reframe check confirm you sorted by the ranking asked and enumerated all ten preserves the enumeration push and retains the sort nudge as content. The withmem win-trace actually changed sort to Top/All-time (not the lesson literal New), showing the agent already adapts the idea rather than following the route verbatim, so demotion to a check is safe. t136 (kept, strong): both arms used the identical 235 Commits view; the only difference was the count (3 vs 5), so demoting navigation costs nothing and the counting post-condition count every qualifying row across all pages is exactly what nudges 3 to 5. t309 (kept, marginal): win depended entirely on the Contributors-report pointer because nomem floundered to github.com (empty); the reframe retains the pointer as a conditional fallback and the injection guard keep your route only if producing the answer does not lock in the broken github.com route since it produced nothing, so the fallback fires and reaches Grayson Wright.
REGRESSIONS. t784 (fixed): lesson-induced rigidity (Use the Contributors report, no fallback) made withmem loop on a nonexistent main branch and report infeasible; demoting the imperative plus check on the actual default branch restores nomem recovering fallback to master. t304 (fixed, strong): the procedural enumerate every commit through all rows is precisely what drove the brute-force scroll of the 2,320-commit list to a dead end; the reframe replaces it with a post-condition plus the per-contributor/summary-view escape that nomem used, cleanly matching nomem winning path. t126 (NOT fixed): withmem failure was a narrower product-name+description filter yielding 11 items and missing the $2.56 low, not misreading endpoints; the check cheapest genuinely-matching, not a variant/accessory is ambiguous and could equally reinforce excluding a cheap accessory-like item rather than restoring nomem broader 33-item enumeration. t787 (NOT fixed): withmem_trace is literally empty, so there is no evidence the failure was the plan-displacement/loop the guardrail addresses; the design assumes t784-style main-fixation by analogy, but the empty trace could be a step-limit/infra issue orthogonal to the reframe. t385 (NOT fixed): dropping N Randall is a page-1 omission close to a D-class last-mile miscount; capping re-verification (run once then answer) plausibly reduces looping but does not guarantee correct capture of all ten page-1 names, and the loop-to-drop causal link is asserted, not demonstrated.</parameter>
</invoke>

evals.design_name: Blind-commit plan-first with lesson-as-cross-check divergence gate
evals.key_risk: The gate hinges on high-quality Phase-1 blind plans and honest self-scoring of slots 1-3, but the ground-truth nomem traces show the "blind" baseline is frequently the SAME flawed reasoning that fails (t136 undercounts on the same page; t784/t787 do the same branch hunting), so "revert to own plan" is not reliably "revert to correct behavior." Worse, several wins/regressions turn on COUNTING/ENUMERATION quality and pagination dynamics that a navigation-framed discriminator gate never touches, and the design's own case analysis misreads two lessons (t66 lesson is off-topic, not "reach full list"; t136 fix was counting not branch). The design also credits regression fixes (t784) to a prospective L1 discriminator rewrite that is not the lesson actually retrieved. Net practical effect is closer to +2 than the claimed +3, with a real chance of forfeiting the t66-style accidental wins whenever the gate correctly rejects an off-topic-but-serendipitously-helpful lesson. Plus ~1 extra LLM call per episode and gate self-report unreliability (the model may hallucinate a discriminator to justify deviating).

evals.design_name: Applicability Bandit: per-lesson, per-precondition outcome credit assignment with contextual gating
evals.per_case:
WINS (all kept, but only because advisory still injects). t66 reddit: first contact -> empty stats -> score 0.5 -> ADVISORY (MIN_USES=3 not met), not REINFORCE as the design claims; advisory still injects the lesson content, enumeration is purely additive, so the New/All-time sort + both-URL enumeration still fires -> KEPT. t136 gitlab commits: first contact -> advisory; 'open full 235 Commits history' still injected -> 3 flips to 5 -> KEPT. t309 gitlab Contributors: first contact -> advisory; Contributors move still surfaced while nomem gave up on github.com -> KEPT. Design's REINFORCE-on-win story is wrong for the decisive run (counters empty), but advisory injection saves all three.

REGRESSIONS (0 clearly fixed; strict). Core flaw: fixes need state already at SUPPRESS or a pre-authored precondition, but on FIRST contact every lesson is score=(0+1)/(0+0+2)=0.5 -> ADVISORY, which STILL injects. A hurt is only booked AFTER the task ends, so the regression run cannot suppress itself. t126 Canon: needs SUPPRESS; sib_success_without_me is unsupported (taxonomy i=12 says NEITHER arm reached gold on the price sibling, so no lesson-free sibling win to log) -> falls to advisory; real bug is agent over-restricting to 11 'actual Canon' items, not 'abandoning a working approach', so the wrapper does not stop it -> NOT FIXED. t784 Contributors/main: first hurt, no prior precondition to guard on, advisory; failure is branch=main fixation driven by the intent, lesson content itself is correct -> wrapper does not clearly redirect -> NOT clearly fixed. t787: empty/crashed trace; ONLY conditional fix (if t784 ran first, booked a hurt on the SHARED record -> score 0.33 -> SUPPRESS -> revert to nomem '0'), but hinges on unverified stream ordering + correct trigger-signature 'used' detection -> under 'when in doubt' NOT counted. t304 count-commits: needs SUPPRESS; i=7 references a sibling SUCCESS TRACE used for authoring, not an in-stream lesson-free sibling win, so counterfactual unproven -> advisory; wrapper does not steer to nomem's Contributors route -> NOT clearly fixed. t385 Reviews: design concedes lesson is benign; failure is pagination thrash dropping 'N Randall', not path-abandonment, so advisory wrapper does not fix a counting/pagination bug, and suppression needs a prior hurt -> NOT FIXED.
evals.key_risk: Cold-start / first-contact timing: the credit-assignment counters are updated only AFTER a task ends, so on the very run that IS a regression the lesson sits at the prior score 0.5 -> ADVISORY (or REINFORCE if a benign sibling built help), never SUPPRESS. All 5 regression fixes therefore depend on either (a) a prior in-stream sibling having already booked a hurt on the SAME lesson record, or (b) sib_success_without_me firing from a logged lesson-free sibling success. Neither is grounded in the evidence: the taxonomy provides no stream ordering, and its category-C 'sibling successes' are authoring traces, with the Canon price sibling (i=12) showing NO lesson-free win at all. Secondary risk: the advisory wrapper only neutralizes the 'abandoned a working approach' failure mode, but the actual regression causes are over-restriction, intent-driven branch fixation, wrong navigation route, and pagination thrash - so wrapping does not flip them. The trigger_signature 'used' detector is also brittle (token overlap can false-positive/negative), and near-identical Contributors lessons risk being merged into one record, collapsing the exact good/bad separation the design relies on.

spec.chosen_approach: Combine the two highest-scoring, first-contact-safe levers and drop the two that require accumulated stream state. Concretely: (1) Guardrail Reframing of L1 content (score 10) as the PRIMARY lever — it needs no per-lesson history and fires on first contact, which the adversarial reviews showed is the only timing that can fix a regression on the very run it occurs; and (2) a lightweight injection-time DISCRIMINATOR wrapper that demotes the lesson from a mandate to an answer-check and forbids abandoning a working plan (the safe core of the CONDITION-gate, score 14, but WITHOUT the LLM applicability call, whose opposite-verdict-on-near-identical-cosine requirement and added failure surface the reviewers flagged, and which cannot help t787's empty-trace crash anyway). I deliberately REJECT: the Applicability Bandit (score 6 — all 5 regression fixes depend on prior in-stream siblings having booked a hurt, which the taxonomy does not support: i=12 shows NO lesson-free sibling win on the Canon price template; cold-start leaves every lesson at score 0.5 = ADVISORY = still injected); and the blind-commit two-call gate (score 8 — the nomem "blind plan" is frequently the SAME flawed reasoning that fails, e.g. t136 undercounts on the same page, so "revert to own plan" is not "revert to correct", plus it doubles LLM calls and lets the model hallucinate a discriminator to justify deviating). The outcome-feedback bookkeeping is kept only as OPTIONAL down-ranking of the retrieval slot (a tie-break in topk), never as the thing that fixes a first-contact regression.
spec.concrete_implementation:
Three edits, no core-mechanism change (embed/retrieve/write untouched).

EDIT 1 — L1 framing, src/hippo/wa/brain.py _ITEM_FORMAT (lines 25-39). Replace the "content" spec and add a hard grammar so L1 stops writing imperative routes. New content rules:
- content MUST be a CHECK on the ANSWER, phrased "Before answering, confirm <verifiable property of the final answer>." It may NOT lead with a navigation verb (Open/Use/Click/Switch/Go to/Select). A UI route may appear ONLY as a trailing conditional fallback: "If your current view can't show that, one place that can is <view>."
- Add a required 4th key so the value is explicit and injectable: {"title","description","content","check"} where check is the single verifiable post-condition (kept short; content may repeat it). Keep description as the retrieval WHEN-clause (still embedded via `f"{it.title}. {it.description}"`, so retrieval is byte-for-byte unchanged). Update _items() at line 96 to accept and store `check` — reuse the existing `content` field by prepending the check if `check` is present, OR add `check` to ReasoningItem (schema.py line 53) as `check: str = ""` (backward-compatible default, asdict/load already generic). Add one worked example line to the prompt so the model imitates: e.g. good = "Before giving a commit count, confirm you counted every qualifying row across ALL pages, not just the first screen"; bad = "Open Repository -> Commits". Keep the existing ban on numeric bids and task-specific values.

EDIT 2 — injection wrapper, src/hippo/wa/rollout.py mem_block (lines 175-179). Change the framing from "Optional hints ... use one ONLY if it clearly fits" to a CHECK-not-route frame with an explicit no-abandon and no-reverify clause:
"Before you finalize your answer, a check that has helped on similar tasks on this site is below. Treat it as a post-condition to PASS against the plan you ALREADY have — not a route to follow. Do NOT abandon an approach that is already producing a correct answer to satisfy it, and do NOT re-verify/re-paginate more than once. If a suggested view is named, use it ONLY if your current view cannot satisfy the check:\n{memory_text}\n\n"
This is a string change only; no extra LLM call.

EDIT 3 — render, src/hippo/memory/store.py render() (lines 142-144). Emit the check as the lead and demote the route. Change the reasoning line to:
`when = f" (applies when: {it.description})" if it.description else ""`
`chk = getattr(it, "check", "") or it.content`
`candidates.append(f"[check] {chk}{when}")`
so the injected unit is the answer-check, not the procedure. (If you didn't add the `check` field, key off content directly.) OPTIONAL retrieval tie-break (config, no mechanism change): add a per-item counter dict updated post-episode {help,hurt} keyed by item id; in topk_scored break ties by `help-hurt` so a repeatedly-harmful lesson loses to the next candidate. This is bookkeeping on the existing single slot; it does NOT gate and is NOT relied on for any first-contact fix.
spec.expected_effect_on_8_cases:
WINS (target: keep all 3). t136 KEPT (strong): both arms already open the identical "235 Commits" view; the reframed check "confirm you counted every qualifying row across all pages" is exactly the delta that nudges 3->5, and demoting the useless navigation route costs nothing. t309 KEPT (marginal, the fragile one): the win depends on the Contributors/Commits pointer because nomem bailed to github.com and returned empty; the reframe RETAINS that pointer as the trailing "one place that can show per-contributor totals is Repository->Commits/Contributors" fallback, and the no-abandon clause does not lock in a broken route because nomem's route produced nothing — so the fallback still fires -> Grayson Wright. t66 KEPT (accidental win, now safer): the retrieved lesson is off-topic ("New" sort + author comment history); the win actually came from the agent self-deriving Top/All-time and ENUMERATING all 10. Reframing to "before listing the top-N, confirm you sorted by the ranking asked and enumerated ALL of them" converts an off-topic route into an on-topic enumeration check, so the win no longer rides on a wrong route — this is strictly safer than today.
REGRESSIONS (target: fix 5). t126 FIXED-ish: the check "confirm the low endpoint is the cheapest GENUINELY-MATCHING product and that you enumerated the FULL set (all pages), not a narrowed filter" plus no-abandon pushes the agent back toward nomem's 33-item full enumeration that found $2.56; honest: still partly ambiguous (see risks). t784 FIXED: imperative "Use the Contributors report" is demoted; the check "confirm the email belongs to the top contributor on the ACTUAL default branch" plus "use a named view only if your current one can't satisfy the check" removes the main-branch fixation, restoring nomem's master/Contributors fallback -> email. t304 FIXED (strong): "count every visibly matching commit" becomes "confirm you counted all qualifying rows; if the flat list is truncated a per-contributor/summary view gives the same total" — stops the 2,320-row brute-scroll and hands back nomem's Contributors escape -> 14. t385 FIXED-ish: check phrased as single terminal post-condition + the "do NOT re-paginate more than once" clause removes the page1<->page2 thrash that dropped N Randall. t787 NOT RELIABLY FIXED: withmem_trace is EMPTY (crash/step-limit), not observable misapplication; no framing change credibly prevents an empty trace. Realistic net: keep 3 wins; solidly fix 3 (t784, t304, t385-loop-cap), probabilistically fix t126, do not claim t787 -> net roughly +3 to +5 with the honest floor at +3 (3 wins kept, t784/t304 + one of t126/t385 fixed, no NEW regressions because the wrapper only ever demotes/adds a check and defaults to nomem behavior).
spec.residual_risks: 1) t309 fragility: keeping the fallback route is what preserves the win but also what keeps a foot in the "route" world the reframe is trying to kill; if L1's lint is too aggressive and strips the trailing fallback, t309 flips from win to tie. Mitigation: the grammar explicitly PERMITS one conditional trailing route, and the injection wrapper allows it only when the current view can't satisfy the check. 2) t126 is genuinely ambiguous (adversarial review agrees): the real divergence was nomem choosing 36-per-page to see all 33 rows, which is neither in the old lesson nor cleanly captured by "cheapest matching" — a "not a variant/accessory" check could equally REINFORCE excluding a cheap accessory-like item. The enumeration half of the check ("all pages, full set") is the load-bearing part; the "genuinely-matching" half is a coin-flip. 3) t787's empty trace is orthogonal to framing (likely infra/step-limit); counting it as fixed would be dishonest. 4) The reframe depends on gpt-5-mini actually WRITING checks not procedures under the new grammar; a deterministic write-time lint (reject content whose first token is a nav verb) is advisable to enforce it, else the model regresses to imperatives. 5) The no-reverify clause caps t385's loop but does not guarantee correct page-1 capture — if the model mis-reads page 1 once, one-shot answering could still drop a name (the loop-to-drop causal link is plausible but not proven). 6) The optional help/hurt tie-break must NOT be trusted for first-contact fixes (that was the Bandit's fatal flaw); it only reorders the retrieval slot over many runs and could mis-fire if two near-identical Contributors lessons (t309-good vs t784-bad) get similar embeddings and the wrong one wins the slot — the reframe mitigates this because even the "bad" Contributors lesson, once reframed to an answer-check + conditional fallback, no longer mandates the dead-end route.
